title: Gooseberry Jam
subtitle: Tart, bright preserve with a natural firm set
excerpt: Gooseberries are loaded with pectin and set readily without added acid. The result is a vivid, sharp preserve that cuts through cream and cheesecake. Makes about three 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (Project Gutenberg #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Gooseberry is among the highest-pectin fruits in the British larder.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze raw topped-and-tailed gooseberries for use out of season.

content.text: Gooseberry jam sets more firmly than almost any other summer preserve,  the berries are so high in pectin that a brief boil is enough to pull a hard set. The flavour is sharp and clean, somewhere between a tart apple and a green grape, and it goes particularly well with cream cheese and cold roast meats. Makes about three 450 g jars.

Put the gooseberries and water in the jam pan over medium heat. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the skins burst and the fruit is completely soft, about 10 minutes. Mash lightly if you want a smoother texture.

Add the sugar and stir over low heat until fully dissolved. Raise to a full rolling boil and cook for 8 to 12 minutes, testing on a cold plate from 8 minutes. Gooseberry jam sets fast. When the surface wrinkles, take the pan off the heat, skim, rest 5 minutes, then ladle into hot sterilised jars and seal.

items.cause: Very high pectin from underripe or early-season fruit, combined with a long boil.
items.fix: Check the set from 8 minutes. Use the jam as it is, over-set gooseberry jam is still delicious, just firm.

items.cause: Prolonged cooking destroys the green pigment.
items.fix: A fast hard boil under 12 minutes keeps the vivid colour. Colour change is not a safety issue.

items.cause: Gooseberries have small, soft seeds that stay in during cooking.
items.fix: Pass the cooked fruit through a sieve before adding the sugar for a seed-free version.

items.cause: Jars were not fully sterilised or the seal was incomplete.
items.fix: Discard and re-make. Sterilise jars in the oven at 120 °C for 20 minutes and fill to within 5 mm of the rim.

content.text: 12 months sealed in a cool, dark cupboard. Refrigerate once opened, use within 4 weeks.
